title: Zeno's Paradoxes: How Can Motion Be Impossible?
question: If you must cross half a distance before crossing the whole of it, and half of that half before that, how does anyone ever arrive anywhere?
summary: Twenty-five centuries ago, Zeno of Elea argued that motion is an illusion by chopping any journey into an infinite number of steps. The paradox looks childish until you try to say exactly why it's wrong.
